english.notes:
(i) A generator of purported intimate images is something used for creating or facilitating the creation of purported intimate images of a person (section 66I(2) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003). This is often referred to as a nudification tool.
(ii) A person would have a defence where they can prove that they took all the reasonable steps to prevent the thing being used to create non-consensual intimate images (section 66I(4)).
(iii) Section 66J provides additional defences for persons charged with this offence, including where: the person carried out the act constituting the offence for the purposes of the prevention, detection, or investigation of crime, or for the purposes of criminal proceedings, in any part of the world;the person proves that they were a member of the Security Service, the Secret Intelligence Service, or GCHQ (a “security body”), and carried out the act for the purposes of the exercise of any function of that security body;the person proves that they were a member of OFCOM, were employed or engaged by OFCOM, or were assisting OFCOM in the exercise of its online safety functions and carried out the act for the purposes of OFCOM’s exercise of those functions.(iv) Section 66K outlines circumstances in which an internet service provider will not commit the offence.
(v) Section 66L provides for corporate liability outlining that where this offence is committed by a body, and is shown to have been committed with the consent or connivance of a relevant person (or a person purporting to act in that capacity), that individual is also guilty of the offence and liable to prosecution.
(vi) Extra-territorial jurisdiction: section 72(1) applies to acts committed outside England and Wales if the conduct would constitute an offence under this section if done within the jurisdiction.
(vii) A person makes, adapts, supplies, or offers to supply a thing for use as a generator of purported intimate images if a reasonable person (having regard to all the circumstances) would consider that they do so (section 66I(3)).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine
Indictment: maximum 3 years imprisonment and/or a fine
The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates' court, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022
